introduction_markdown: This paper is arranged in two sections, A and B. Answer ALL questions in Sections A and B. Section A: Answer ALL the questions in the spaces provided (10 questions); the mark allocation for each question is indicated. Section B: Answer ALL FOUR questions; all questions in Section B carry equal marks (15 marks each). You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Non-programmable calculators are allowed. Duration: two and a half hours.
incertitudes: Q B3 : barème imprimé par bloc ((i) 10 marks, (ii) 5 marks) ; les parties (i)(a)-(d) sont numérotées a à d et (ii)(a)-(c) numérotées e à g. « fg(x) » est lu comme f(g(x)) (convention usuelle).

Q B3 (ii) : construction à réaliser par l'élève (aucune figure imprimée) ; le corrigé décrit les étapes. S peut être placé de part ou d'autre de PQ : la longueur MS = 4 cm sert de référence (PS = 5 cm, PM = 3 cm).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Given the functions $f$ and $g$ such that $f:x\mapsto2x+3$ and $g:x\mapsto x-1$.

Find,

a) $f(-2)$

questions.corrige_markdown:
Write $y=x-1$ and make $x$ the subject: $x=y+1$.

Swap the letters: $g^{-1}(x)=x+1$.

Check: $g(g^{-1}(x))=(x+1)-1=x$.

**Answer: $g^{-1}(x)=x+1$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: d) the value of $x$, for which $f(x)=g(x)$. *[10 marks for (i)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Set $f(x)=g(x)$: $2x+3=x-1$.

Collect the terms in $x$ on the left and the numbers on the right: $2x-x=-1-3$, so $x=-4$.

Check: $f(-4)=2(-4)+3=-5$ and $g(-4)=-4-1=-5$.

**Answer: $x=-4$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii) Using only a pencil, ruler and a pair of compasses,

a) Draw the line $PQ=6$ cm
questions.corrige_markdown: Using the ruler, draw a straight line segment and mark the points $P$ and $Q$ on it exactly $6$ cm apart.

questions.enonce_markdown: b) Construct the perpendicular bisector of $PQ$ to meet $PQ$ at $M$
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. With the compasses set to a radius larger than $3$ cm (half of $PQ$), for example $4$ cm, and centre $P$, draw one arc above $PQ$ and one arc below $PQ$.
2. Keeping the same radius and with centre $Q$, draw two more arcs that cut the first two arcs.
3. Join the two points where the arcs cross with a ruler. This line is the perpendicular bisector of $PQ$.
4. Mark $M$ where this line meets $PQ$: $M$ is the mid-point of $PQ$, so $PM=MQ=3$ cm.

Leave all construction arcs visible.

questions.enonce_markdown: c) Draw the line $PS=5$ cm, where $S$ is a point on the perpendicular bisector *[5 marks for (ii)]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Set the compasses to a radius of $5$ cm.
2. With centre $P$, draw an arc that cuts the perpendicular bisector. Call the intersection $S$.
3. Join $P$ to $S$ with the ruler: $PS=5$ cm.

Check by calculation: triangle $PMS$ has a right angle at $M$, $PM=3$ cm and $PS=5$ cm, so $MS=\sqrt{5^2-3^2}=\sqrt{16}=4$ cm. When you measure $MS$ on your drawing you should find $4$ cm. ($S$ may be taken above or below $PQ$.)
